sources.collection_name: World War II Army Enlistment Records
sources.rights_notes: No raw row or full private identifier is retained. John R Davis Jr and Lloyd G Davis have exact identifier-and-name agreement. Six- and seven-character index values were not padded. The incomplete Army file is not a comprehensive OSS, officer, Navy, Marine Corps, civilian, women's-service, Coast Guard, or foreign roster; a non-hit is not negative proof.

sources.title: World War II Army Enlistment Records: Code Lists
sources.repository_publisher: National Archives at College Park - Electronic Records
sources.locator: Code No. 30, Civilian Occupations, PDF physical page 171 / printed page XI and physical pages 176-177; entry 1-37 and neighboring x-92 entries visually and textually checked
sources.collection_name: World War II Army Enlistment Records technical documentation
sources.rights_notes: The official table defines 1-37 as Stenographers and typists. It defines 4-92, 6-92, and 8-92 but not 9-92, so value 992 is not interpreted. Occupational categories identify neither an employer, workplace, exact job title, nor the sequence from Army service to OSS.

affiliations.date_precision: Civilian-occupation value 137 was recorded at Army entry on October 30, 1940. NARA's code table defines 1-37 as Stenographers and typists; no employer, workplace, or exact role is identified.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier and full name confirm the Army identity. The historical occupational group is not converted into a named employer, immediate-OSS affiliation, workplace, or narrower role.
